messages:
lee: hi folks — was hospitalized in oregon while traveling last week. insurer denied as non-emergency/out-of-network and left me with a $1,200 balance. what paperwork do i need to appeal?

hana: ugh sorry that happened. please upload the EOB, itemized hospital bill, admission/discharge summary, and any triage/ER notes. also a photo of your insurance card.

lee: uploaded EOB + bill (links): https://files.example/eob-lee-0412.pdf https://files.example/bill-0412.pdf

claims-bot: Appeal checklist: [EOB, itemized bill, admission/discharge summary, ER/triage notes, front/back insurance card, signed patient statement]. Standard review 30-60 days; request expedited review with clinical note if short-term financial hardship.

broker-sam: if it was an emergency, federal/state laws often require coverage regardless of in-network status (prudent layperson standard). include the discharge summary and a provider note stating emergency evaluation. i'll flag our broker contact to request internal review.

lee: how should i write the patient statement?

hana: short template: 
"I, Lee P., was seen at Cascade Regional Hospital on 04/12/2025 for acute chest pain and shortness of breath. I presented my insurance card at registration and sought immediate medical attention. Based on symptoms and medical assessment, the visit met emergency care criteria. I request reconsideration of the denial and reprocessing as in-network/emergency services."

billing-bot: Also try asking hospital billing to re-submit with emergency place-of-service code and the treating taxonomy/NPI on claim. If hospital rebills, insurer will reprocess.

lee: thanks — sending docs to benefits@redwood.com with subject "APPEAL: Lee P. 04/12/2025" now. appreciate the help.

hana: got it. i'll coordinate with sam for broker escalation if insurer holds. keep this thread updated when you get confirmation. :thumbsup:
